text: The review decision codes and the final-call values are reference rows in force and never constants: the attach record keeps the legacy code DOCATT that RWB-P5-E1054-CON already declares, the review completion of a confirm or a correct carries its own code from LOV-DECISION, and the final call carries the review outcome in force (ATTACHED, DISCARDED, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED).
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives decision_log_entry a decision_code from LOV-DECISION and a final_call, T3.2 enumerates neither, and the record must still be assertable, groupable and reproducible.
read: RWB-E1-054 section 4 step 7, section 8 BR6 and BR9; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-014 and DF-DEC-015 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; RWB-P5-E1054-CON sections 12.3 and 14.
confirm: Solution architect with the P7 business analyst and the reference-data owner
impact: Medium: the codes become reference rows, so a new review decision code is a data change and no scenario changes.

text: The review facts of an entry sit in the record's own columns and payload: inputs_ref carries the review item ID, case_id carries the case of the item where it has one, and actions and outcome carry documentRef, reviewStatus, reviewOutcome and fieldCount; no review column and no review field ID is added to decision_log_entry.
why: The TSD gives actions and outcome as jsonb with no key list and no review-specific column, so the placement is a contract convention that must be stated once to be assertable.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-014 and DF-DEC-015; RWB-E1-054 sections 4 and 11; RWB-P5-E1054-CON section 12.3 (the type, the item ID, the reviewer) and BR8 of that contract (no field value in the record).
confirm: Solution architect with the document hub contract owner
impact: Medium: a rename touches the validator and the two indexes only, because no column depends on it.

text: The alert for a review decision that never arrives stays with the generic missing-record alert of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; this story adds no second alert, no reconciliation sweep and no Schedule, and its own refusals are reported through the exception queue and the LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED incident.
why: Architecture v5 slide 28 gives the ledger one missing-record alert, FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-026-05 gives one incident name, and two overlapping alerts on one gap would raise the same case twice.
read: Architecture v5 slides 28 and 44 through the P7 context pack; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-026-05 and AC-EXC-P7-026-06; TSD P7 v2 NFR-035; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10.
confirm: Solution architect with the observability and Compliance owners
impact: Low: the target and the incident already exist and one owner raises them.

text: The ledger of this service has no REST write path and no REST read declared here: the two decision-log reads of the Ownership Map are RWB-P7-E2005-APP's, the append is the consumer's transaction, and this story adds no operation to base /api/recovery/decision/v1.
why: The Ownership Map gives P7 two GET paths only, and a private append path would become a second writer of the ledger beside the ingest.
read: P7 context pack ownership rows (GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId}) and the 19 operations listed; TSD P7 v2 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-13.
confirm: Solution architect with the Ownership Map owner
impact: Low: the slice is complete on the consumer and the two reads answer what the consumer appends.

text: The service identity is named 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' until the ACE team allocates it with the schema rwb_decision; the story never uses the shared monolith login.
why: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and no document states its name.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules.
impact: Low: a name only, recorded in the platform secret store.

text: A refusal or an undeliverable envelope is retried four times in all, then goes to the exception queue with owner RW-PLATADM and reason 'review item not found', 'outcome mismatch', 'no answer in the budget' or 'store unavailable', and one incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED is raised for it; a replay appends the entry once.
why: The FSD gives the four attempts, the exception queue and the incident name and not the reason strings, and the reasons must be assertable in the tests.
read: FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-026-05 and AC-EXC-P7-026-06; TSD P7 v2 T7 NFR-077 and NFR-078; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09.
confirm: Solution architect with the platform administrator
impact: Low: no behaviour changes; the reason values are the operator's filter.

text: The eight patterns of the Work Package add platform contract rows RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the consumed contracts RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P5-E1054-CON; the metadata rows stay exactly as the Work Package fixes them, so Depends on (build) is None and RWB-P5-E1054-CON is the only contract dependency, and every added row is carried in the pattern table and the fakes of section 13 and 12.8.
why: The Work Package fixes empty H and one C row for this secondary slice while the DP table of Template and Rules R5.5 adds five platform contracts and one reference-data contract that must still be named and faked.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 (DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.7; Work Package B2-P7-015 story line (H [], C [RWB-P5-E1054-CON], I [], X [], secondary true).
confirm: Delivery lead with the solution architect
impact: Low: the metadata rows are authoritative and the added contracts arrive as platform CON work, so the lane is unaffected.
